verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance documents OAuth client-credentials for server-to-server use, with one-time-shown secrets and rotation. Write capabilities (create, update, delete) are gated and must be explicitly granted by Harbor to the account, which suggests a read-by-default privilege tier, but there is no evidence that users can scope individual credentials themselves. missing for 10: user-defined per-credential scopes or permissions, multiple distinct credentials per agent, resource-level restriction, self-service privilege configuration, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Client Credentials — For server-to-server integrations. Exchange your client ID and secret at /api/v3/oauth/access_token with grant_type=client_credentials
Creating, updating, and deleting resources requires additional capabilities which Harbor Compliance must explicitly grant to your account
The secret is shown only once; if you lose it, rotate it to get a new one.
